subtopic: Adding equations and completing the square

problem.text: The parabolas $y = x^2 + 15x + 32$ and $x = y^2 + 49y + 593$ meet at one point $(x_0, y_0)$. Find $x_0 + y_0$.

steps.title: Where to start: add the two equations
steps.body: Solving by substitution would give a degree-4 equation, which is painful. But one equation has an $x^2$ and the other a $y^2$, so adding them puts both squares in one equation, where we can complete the square in $x$ and in $y$ at the same time. The point $(x_0, y_0)$ satisfies both equations, so it satisfies their sum.

your_turn.prompt: Add the equations $y = x^2 + 15x + 32$ and $x = y^2 + 49y + 593$, and move everything to one side.

steps.title: Complete the square in each variable
steps.body: We have $x^2 + 14x = (x+7)^2 - 49$ and $y^2 + 48y = (y+24)^2 - 576$. The constant $625$ is exactly $49 + 576$, which is the sign that this is the right move.

your_turn.prompt: Substitute these into $x^2 + 14x + y^2 + 48y + 625 = 0$ and simplify.

steps.title: A sum of squares equal to zero
steps.body: The square of a real number is never negative. So if two squares add to $0$, neither can be positive, and both must be $0$. That pins down $x_0$ and $y_0$ exactly. Careful: adding the equations only gives a condition the point must satisfy, so check the point on both parabolas.

your_turn.answer: No. $(y+24)^2$ can never be $-3$, because squares of real numbers are at least $0$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: So $x_0 + 7 = 0$ and $y_0 + 24 = 0$, giving $x_0 = -7$ and $y_0 = -24$. Check: $49 - 105 + 32 = -24$ and $576 - 1176 + 593 = -7$, so the point is on both parabolas. Then $x_0 + y_0 = -7 + (-24) = -31$. The answer is $-31$.
